2016.emphasis_summary: Excerpts are mostly governance boilerplate (Corporate Governance Guidelines, NYSE website-disclosure rules, Compensation Committee independence) plus the 2015 non-financial bonus scorecard (customer allegiance, e-business launch, $90 million in Life Technologies revenue synergies), with no diversity or environmental text captured.
2016.notable_shifts: First available year in sample; no prior-year comparison.

2017.emphasis_summary: The excerpts repeat the governance and compensation boilerplate, with human capital limited to a recap of e-business integration and revenue-growth positioning and still no diversity or environmental text captured.
2017.notable_shifts: Little substantive change from 2016: the governance and compensation text is largely repeated, and the only new human-capital content is the 2016 performance recap ('Positioning the Company for Accelerated Revenue Growth').

2018.emphasis_summary: The excerpts center on the first CEO pay-ratio disclosure (an estimated CEO-to-median-employee ratio of 324 to 1) and governance rules such as a director retirement age of 72, with still no diversity or environmental text captured.
2018.notable_shifts: The new items are the pay-ratio disclosure and a recap of leadership-diversity progress and FEI synergy targets; the governance text is otherwise carried over from 2017.

2019.emphasis_summary: For the first time the excerpts populate the diversity and environmental sections, covering Board Diversity and Board Tenure, a Charitable Giving Program, and shareholder engagement on environmental and social matters.
2019.notable_shifts: Much of the apparent jump reflects extraction, since diversity_dei and environment_sustainability were empty in 2016-2018 and now return text; the substantive additions are board diversity and tenure policy language and CSR items such as the Little Scientists program.

2020.emphasis_summary: The excerpts emphasize talent and inclusion, featuring Employee Resource Groups for attracting, developing and retaining diverse talent, board diversity and tenure, and a director skills matrix.
2020.notable_shifts: DEI and talent language roughly doubles from 2019, with the Employee Resource Group language and the director skills matrix as the new elements.

2021.emphasis_summary: COVID-19 framing takes over the excerpts, including a virtual-meeting notice tied to the pandemic and a CEO message about 'the greatest health crisis', alongside largely unchanged board-diversity and governance boilerplate.
2021.notable_shifts: COVID-19 mentions rise from about 4 to 9 and the pandemic becomes the lead framing in place of the 2020 talent emphasis, while the board-diversity and governance text carries over.

2022.emphasis_summary: The excerpts lead with ESG, including a commitment to carbon neutrality by 2050 that builds on a 30% greenhouse-gas reduction goal, alongside a Forbes female-friendly ranking and a 100% Human Rights Campaign LGBTQ+ workplace equality score.
2022.notable_shifts: This is the first year the environment excerpt contains concrete climate targets rather than general sustainability language, and the excerpts add recognition-based DEI claims (Forbes and HRC rankings) that appear in no other TMO year.

2023.emphasis_summary: Climate and renewable energy lead, with power purchasing agreements to reach 100% renewable energy for U.S. operations, a reduced carbon footprint claim, and a Board diversity section promising enhanced disclosure on diversity, refreshment and tenure.
2023.notable_shifts: The 2023 excerpts move from 2022's long-range carbon-neutrality goal to near-term operating steps (power purchasing agreements for U.S. renewable energy) and add the enhanced Board diversity, refreshment and tenure disclosure, while the 2022 Forbes and HRC recognition claims are gone.

2024.emphasis_summary: Operational integrity and a climate-and-nature framing lead, with commitments to ethical, quality, safety and sourcing standards and an approach to climate, nature and sustainable product design rooted in global frameworks.
2024.notable_shifts: The 2024 excerpts broaden the 2023 climate language into nature and sustainable product design and add an operational-standards narrative (ethics, quality, safety, sourcing), while the Board diversity section is mostly table-of-contents text, so little new board content is captured.
